reasoning: Recent polling (February 2026) shows TISZA leading Fidesz 55%-35% among decided voters, with 42%-31% among all voters. A 2/3 supermajority requires 133 of 199 seats. Hungary's electoral system magnifies majoritarian advantages through 'winner compensation,' potentially converting ~45-50% vote share into supermajorities. However, TISZA needs to translate its 42% support into 133+ seats. Analyst estimates suggest TISZA could achieve a 2/3 majority with current polling leads. Key uncertainties: (1) 27% undecided voters could shift outcomes; (2) Fidesz's structural advantages (constituency design, diaspora votes ~94% for Fidesz); (3) polling accuracy (Median is reliable but pro-government polls show different results); (4) voter mobilization (97% TISZA vs 85% Fidesz turnout certainty favors opposition). The electoral system's magnification effect and TISZA's substantial lead make a supermajority plausible, but Fidesz's institutional advantages and remaining uncertainty warrant moderate confidence.
